author: Codex assessment agent /root/liberal_conservative (AI-assisted doctrinal interpretation)
changeNote: Completed 240 independently considered answers to the current bank from the scoped doctrine. No imported 12Axes vectors or score targets. User authorised neutral answers and completion on 2026-10-04. Conditional modern applications and mixed-causation modelling are explicitly inferred, not claims of direct statements or scientific findings. Independent review completed on 2026-10-04; question-meaning and evidence corrections are recorded in review notes.

metadata.name: Liberalism
metadata.description: International constitutional liberalism anchored in the 1947 Oxford Manifesto, with market institutions, civil rights and representative democracy. Distinct from social liberalism and strict minimal-state liberalism.
metadata.scope: International constitutional liberalism anchored in the 1947 Oxford Manifesto, with market institutions, civil rights and representative democracy. Distinct from social liberalism and strict minimal-state liberalism. This is a representative interpretation of the specified doctrine, not answers personally submitted by every adherent. Modern technological questions apply the doctrine conditionally. Trait-specific neutral responses express a stated mixed-causation model where the doctrine rejects a single fixed causal priority; they are not empirical scientific estimates.
metadata.phrase: A society protecting individual rights, representative government and private enterprise within constitutional limits.

sources.title: John Stuart Mill on Human Nature, Self-interest, and Institutional Incentives

axes.brief: Constitutional consent and protected opposition constrain executive authority; participation does not require direct democracy.
axes.counterEvidence: The manifesto safeguards minorities as well as majority consent; referendums cannot override basic rights.

answers.rationale: Office depends on continuing electoral consent, not personal entitlement.
Expert advice cannot replace citizens' political equality.
Equal citizenship rules out educational tests for suffrage.
Executive lawmaking against parliament breaches constitutional consent.
Political liberty requires genuinely competitive opposition parties.
Public accountability includes scrutiny by those outside government.
Independent justice must enforce limits on governmental power.
Occupational organisations cannot substitute for the general electorate.
Incumbents cannot monopolise the ballot by excluding dissent.
Popular repeal is acceptable within minority-rights safeguards.
Constitutional government distributes rather than personalises decision-making.
Removal for abuse gives practical effect to accountability.
Unilateral postponement destroys the requirement of free consent.
Defined recall can reinforce consent, with procedural protections.
Unaccountable leadership contradicts the state's instrumental role.
Military substitution denies civilian citizens their political agency.

axes.brief: Personal autonomy carries duties to others, with independent courts policing coercion.
axes.counterEvidence: Public protection can justify restrictions; a liberty commitment does not forbid every warrant or safety rule.

answers.rationale: Self-regarding adult risk falls within protected personal choice.
A specific judicial warrant reconciles investigation and privacy.
Limited disruption is proportionate to meaningful political expression.
Offence alone cannot extinguish criticism of public institutions.
Paternalistic compulsion needs more than protecting competent adults.
Routine years-long tracking dispenses with individual justification.
Danger to other road users supports narrowly targeted testing.
Preventive protection and liberty conflict; necessity and review decide.
Moral disapproval alone cannot justify suppressing adult reading.
Anonymous association remains protected absent particular wrongdoing.
Area-wide suspicion is weaker than an individualised justification.
Credible serious disorder supplies an external-harm justification.
Judicial control protects the home against arbitrary intrusion.
Exposing misconduct serves accountability, subject to concrete safety harms.
Self-defence and public safety require proportionate licensing, not a blanket rule.
Indefinite executive detention abolishes independent legal protection.

axes.brief: The Oxford text expressly respects minority language, faith and customs alongside common democratic duties.
axes.counterEvidence: Recognition need not give every cultural demand priority or exempt conduct from generally necessary safety rules.

answers.rationale: National customs cannot automatically override equal minority liberties.
Reasonable accommodation makes equal access effective rather than merely formal.
Common civic obligations do not require wholesale cultural adoption.
Minority identity is compatible with membership in the polity.
A common working language and accessible services both matter.
Recognition includes small minorities rather than numerical exclusion.
Public cultural support should not systematically subordinate minorities.
Distinct identities cannot categorically displace common civic obligations.
Reasonable scheduling accommodation follows respect for minority faiths.
Plural traditions fit the manifesto's explicit minority protections.
Civic participation is compatible with retaining distinct customs.
Useful multilingual signs can remove practical access barriers.
Families retain freedom to balance national and communal attachments.
Religious accommodation is balanced against genuinely general safety restrictions.
National membership need not require cultural uniformity.
Integration should secure participation rather than prescribe private customs.

axes.brief: Freedom of movement and equal personhood favour accessible migration with lawful administration.
axes.counterEvidence: Travel freedom is not an unconditional settlement guarantee; capacity and protection obligations can conflict.

answers.rationale: Flexible capacity planning is preferable to rigid numerical closure.
Improving one's life is a legitimate reason to migrate.
Skill exclusivity would exclude family and humanitarian claims.
Family unity gives settled migrants a substantial admission claim.
Protection need should outweigh productivity or cultural likeness.
Residence decisions require individual circumstances, not automatic immunity or deportation.
Voluntary employment supports admission absent compelling capacity harms.
Housing pressures and mobility rights require contextual balancing.
Family unity warrants flexibility beyond a single economic quota.
Employment supplies a strong practical basis for entry.
Independent resources or protection needs also justify residence.

Graduation can provide a conditional route to residence because education and voluntary opportunity support integration. Such a route is different from guaranteed residence and can still include ordinary legal checks.
Urgent protection should not be extinguished by ordinary quotas.
Cultural resemblance is an unequal basis for admission.
Lawful residents need basic social security on fair terms.
Diversity is welcome, but cultural difference alone is not an admission entitlement.

axes.brief: International law and cooperation seek peace while allowing collective defence of liberty.
axes.counterEvidence: The manifesto's peace aspiration does not mean abandoning allies or prohibiting every preventive defence.

answers.rationale: Interests alone are insufficient without defence or collective-law justification.
Peaceful resolution should precede coercive international action.
Adequate defence matters; superiority at substantial cost is context-dependent.
Well-evidenced imminence can justify necessary preventive defence.
Collective enforcement and humanitarian emergencies complicate a defence-only rule.
Compulsory service requires stronger necessity than general deterrence.
Reasonable concessions are preferable to avoidable destructive war.
Efficiency alone cannot replace accountability for lethal targeting.
Defending people takes priority over discretionary foreign campaigns.
Absolute abstention would abandon collective protection against aggression.
External capability may support lawful alliances but is not intrinsically required.
Unresolved territorial claims do not justify initiating war.
Threats need lawful protective grounds beyond bargaining advantage.
Preventing avoidable conflict usually outweighs symbolic demonstrations.
Legitimate intelligence and risks of escalation need proportional judgment.
Verifiable mutual reductions can strengthen collective security.

axes.brief: Oxford internationalism supports enforceable freely undertaken obligations and an equitable world organisation.
axes.counterEvidence: Consent matters, but freely joining rules cannot mean ignoring each adverse judgment.

answers.rationale: International obligations can legitimately limit domestic discretion.
Agreed international procedures may bind dissenting member governments.
Domestic courts should respect valid international legal commitments.
Durable collective security necessarily involves mutual constraints.
Treaty exit rules and sovereign consent both require respect.
Equal international law includes review of government officials.
Immediate interests do not automatically trump agreed common duties.
Cross-border harms justify jointly authorised environmental decisions.
Shared foreign-policy institutions are permissible when voluntarily joined.
Universal liberties justify agreed external rights supervision.
Currency arrangements depend on accountable design and economic conditions.
Shared problems warrant pooled resources and decision-making.
Consensual border cooperation is compatible with national democracy.
Agreed common rules enable reliable free exchange.
A democratic federation is possible, but not obligatory for every country.
Upholding agreed law can outweigh short-term national advantage.

axes.brief: Private enterprise is the default; public ownership is permissible where competition fails.
axes.counterEvidence: Oxford explicitly rejects private monopolies as well as state monopolisation; utilities differ from competitive firms.

answers.rationale: Competitive private enterprise is a core economic liberty.
Monopoly networks meet Oxford's exception to private provision.
Comparable outcomes leave the presumption favouring private choice.
Competitive industries do not normally meet the public-ownership exception.
Clinical provision depends on access and competition, not ownership alone.
A monopoly rail network supports the exceptional public role.
Equal access and lower cost support competitive contracting.
A public bank needs an identified gap beyond mere duplication.
Competitive commercial assets generally belong outside government ownership.
Housing access matters, but tenure mix requires local evidence.
Effective regulation removes the need for state ownership.
Resources alone do not establish that competition is impossible.
Routine contestable services can use private suppliers.
Strategic necessity matters more than sale revenue alone.
Persistent failure strengthens the case for private restructuring.
Public-interest broadcasting can coexist with protected independent media.

axes.brief: Oxford explicitly supports exchange without protective trade barriers.
axes.counterEvidence: Security and monopoly concerns can qualify openness; retaliatory protection is not an end in itself.

answers.rationale: Shielding producers from competition frustrates consumers' freedom.
Open exchange takes priority over incumbent sales protection.
Nationality alone should not outweigh value for taxpayers.
Private purchasers generally choose the most suitable suppliers.
Essential supplies warrant resilience, not indiscriminate import suppression.
Consumers benefit from lower barriers without identical foreign concessions.
Infant-industry protection risks preserving sectional privilege.
Equal commercial rules should extend to foreign investors.
Farm protection needs a concrete security case beyond producer preference.
Adjustment preserves competition rather than entrenching protected incumbents.
Retaliation restricts exchange and should remain exceptional.
Origin-neutral taxation follows commercial equality.
Subsidy distortions warrant remedies, but broad restrictions harm exchange.
Diversified trade can be preferable to costly self-sufficiency.
Specific security risks may justify screening strategic control.
Digital services inherit the presumption for free international exchange.

axes.brief: Market choice and competition coexist with protection against monopoly and insecurity.
axes.counterEvidence: Oxford's safety-net commitment prevents treating all regulation as illegitimate planning.

answers.rationale: Enterprise entails deciding what goods to offer.
Compulsory output targets substitute administration for competition.
Price discovery normally belongs to market participants.
Public investment can assist gaps without directing the economy.
Consumer choice should discipline ordinary business viability.
Price caps may impair supply; narrow monopoly remedies differ.
Entry should not depend on a government production-needs test.
Politically directed lending threatens independent capital allocation.
Oxford expressly opposes exchange restrictions.
Public goods can justify support, but sectional favouritism cannot.
Monetary innovation requires stability safeguards as well as choice.
A wage floor can support fair conditions without output planning.
Collective and individual negotiation fit complementary labour-capital interests.
Sound monetary institutions should not become production-planning instruments.
Supply incentives generally favour market rents with separate assistance.
Ordinary comprehensive coordination would suppress economic freedom.

axes.brief: Security against social risks is legitimate, while enterprise and property remain protected.
axes.counterEvidence: Oxford promises social security but not equal incomes or a flat-tax doctrine.

answers.rationale: Adequacy and opportunity matter alongside incentives; equalisation is not absolute.
Income disparity alone does not establish an entitlement to others' earnings.
Adequate security can require taxes beyond a subsistence floor.
A safety net fits plural outcomes better than substantial levelling.
Progressive contributions can finance shared social protection fairly.
Lower taxes and adequate security must be weighed together.
Inheritance taxation depends on opportunity, family property and proportionality.
Continuing need cannot simply vanish when a calendar expires.
Wealth taxes require balancing social needs against secure ownership.
Tax convenience alone cannot determine adequate protection.
Responsible citizenship requires more than bare physical survival.
Neither tax cuts nor benefit rises deserve automatic priority.
In-work support can reconcile enterprise with social security.
Equal marginal rates are not required by equal civil rights.
Compensated reform still needs a specific public-interest justification.
Social-risk protection extends beyond immediate destitution.

axes.brief: Liberty of conscience and equal citizenship favour civil political authority.
axes.counterEvidence: Cultural heritage and voluntary worship remain protected; secular government need not suppress religion.

answers.rationale: Public law should be accessible to citizens of every conscience.
One faith cannot possess authoritative legislative privilege.
Elected civil institutions do not require clerical permission.
Constitutional religious privilege risks unequal citizenship.
Education can explain religions without recruiting adherents.
State-directed faith formation conflicts with conscience.
Independent civil law must govern enforceable public judgments.

Freedom of conscience favours religious groups participating on equal civic terms rather than possessing a privileged official role in reviewing legislation. The objection concerns institutional religious privilege, even without a veto.

Religiously inclusive public authority favours official ceremonies without organised worship, while citizens remain free to worship separately. This inference concerns governmental endorsement, not only compulsory attendance.
Promoting belief itself is not a neutral public purpose.
Government should not imply unequal standing between beliefs.
Inherited holidays can be cultural, but explicit religious endorsement complicates them.
Clerical status alone does not supply democratic legitimacy.
Religion-specific fiscal privilege needs more than charitable justification.
Civil marriage should not depend on religious consent.
Voluntary mediation must remain subject to equal civil rights.

axes.brief: Individual choice and sex equality permit social reform without requiring every novelty.
axes.counterEvidence: Family respect in Oxford tempers any inference that liberalism disdains inherited institutions.

answers.rationale: Voluntary social development should not be frozen by the state.
Tradition cannot automatically defeat changing personal convictions.
Equal respect extends beyond one preferred household arrangement.
Assigned roles constrain the manifesto's sex equality.
Equal legal choice supports marriage irrespective of sex; modern inference.
Family stability is valued without necessarily privileging one composition.
Early pregnancy decisions favour personal agency, subject to competing interests.
Parental conscience and children's access to education both matter.
Equal treatment favours judging adoptive parents individually.
Dress conventions should remain voluntary rather than socially compulsory.
Respectful language can adapt through voluntary social practice.
Customs deserve examination rather than inherited priority alone.
Equal rights imply acceptance of individual occupational and social choices.
Consequences matter, but slowness is not intrinsically virtuous.
Understanding diversity supports equal citizenship without compelled belief.
Voluntary heritage preservation is worthwhile without overriding present needs.

axes.brief: Creative freedom supports innovation, while equal rights constrain external and irreversible harms.
axes.counterEvidence: Modern biotechnology answers are conditional applications, not claims of 1947 technological foresight.

answers.rationale: Promising reversible innovation need not await complete certainty.
Trial limits depend on severity and reversibility, not uncertainty alone.
Substantial public benefit can justify proportionate habitat losses.
Medical exposure requires stronger safety evidence than ordinary consumer novelty.
Productivity gains are legitimate with education and social-risk protection.
Habitat preservation is important but not an absolute development veto.
Food innovation and uncertain ecological costs require proportionate evaluation.
Invasive enhancement raises durable risks requiring stronger evidence.
Technology and conservation are complementary rather than universally ranked.
Poorly understood major environmental harm warrants investigation first.
Adult autonomy and irreversible implant risks must be balanced.
Diagnostic reliability protects patients' equal access to competent care.
Research freedom competes with nonconsenting future persons' interests.
Ecosystem exposure justifies evidence beyond yield alone.
Basic housing and mobility needs can justify managed development.
Irreversibility raises the evidential threshold for permissible risk.

axes.brief: Dispersed accountable institutions protect liberty, with common rights and coordination where needed.
axes.counterEvidence: Oxford does not prescribe a constitutional map; the institutional answers are conditional liberal inferences.

answers.rationale: Protected regional competence checks concentrated political power.
Competence disputes require constitutional adjudication, not unilateral national preference.
Self-determination competes with minority rights and negotiated constitutional obligations.
Programme convenience alone should not extinguish protected autonomy.
Regional constitutions permit accountable diversity within common rights.
Dispersed policing can check concentration while allowing cooperation.
Local accountability and equal national opportunity require fiscal balance.
Common rights do not require uniform control of every subject.
Regional tax choice makes local spending democratically accountable.
Basic employment rights can be national while implementation varies.
Local democratic choice should normally govern local arrangements.
Common minimum healthcare rights can coexist with regional additions.
Minority institutions deserve autonomy consistent with individual rights.
Harmful fiscal externalities can justify limited common constraints.
Wholly regional effects favour the closest accountable authority.
Cross-regional disasters justify coordinated national direction with review.

axes.brief: Independent agency, education and opportunity reject deterministic ranking; empirical mechanisms remain plural.
axes.counterEvidence: Neither equal rights nor liberalism proves genetic or environmental percentages. Neutral here represents an explicitly non-reductive model, not a scientific finding.

answers.rationale: Education and community conditions develop responsible individual agency.

International IQ comparisons involve education, health, measurement and inheritance; the scoped doctrine does not assign a stable causal priority. This representative response adopts a mixed model rather than inferring biology from citizenship or tradition.

Oxford rejects imposed unequal rights, while Millian liberalism recognises both individual capacities and the effects of institutions. This model therefore allows socialisation and biology to interact; legal sex equality alone does not prove which explains more behavioural difference.
Biological sensitivity and lived stressors jointly shape responses; no doctrinal primacy.
Varied education and free choice cultivate differentiated interests.
Risk decisions combine disposition, information and learned incentives.
Civic habits develop through participation and reciprocal responsibility.
Empathy can involve both human capacities and cultivated experience.
Attention reflects individual capacities and surroundings; no fixed priority follows.

Independent moral reflection and upbringing can reshape immediate judgments, while human capacities also constrain them. Oxford does not make biological predominance a necessary consequence of agency, so the representative model retains both causal contributions.
Threat perception includes experience and disposition; context determines their weight.
Individuality permits temperament differences without endorsing a single causal ranking.
Personal tastes combine experience and embodied dispositions without a uniform doctrine.

Violence rates can reflect social conditions, institutions and individual dispositions; the doctrine supplies no defensible racial causal ranking. The representative model therefore withholds primacy rather than deriving empirical claims from equal rights.
Learned responsibility is preferable to inherited racial character as explanation.

The representative liberal model treats occupational access and social expectations as causes of earnings differences, so does not attribute the aggregate pay gap to economic contribution instead of those conditions. This is a modest causal inference, not a claim about moral worth.

review.reviewer: Codex independent assessment reviewer /root/socialist_green (separate from author)
review.notes: Independently read all 240 answers against the current bank and checked the scoped primary doctrine plus scholarship/context. No scores or desired locations were consulted. Reviewed literal government authority, ownership versus funding, official religious review versus veto, graduate routes versus guaranteed residence, military initiation versus response, and causal claims versus moral equality. Corrections: culture-nature-16: -1 -> -1; culture-nature-03: 1 -> 0; culture-nature-10: -1 -> 0; restricted-immigration-open-immigration-12: 0 -> -1; secular-religious-08: -2 -> -2; secular-religious-09: 1 -> 1. The inferred modern-policy answers and mixed causal models remain representative applications, not documented answers by every adherent or scientific causal estimates. Similarity review is a subsequent mechanical check. Validation returned zero errors. Explicitly examined neutral-count warnings: public-private 5/16, high-redistribution-low-redistribution 5/16, innovation-caution 5/16, central-local 5/16, culture-nature 11/16. Retained condition-dependent policy tradeoffs and representative interaction models; in particular the Culture vs Nature neutrals withhold causal primacy rather than converting equal rights into empirical proof. High neutrality records weaker doctrinal determination and must not be presented as a precisely measured consensus among adherents. No answers were changed after inspecting validation scores.
